subtopics.title: Inflation Defined and the CPI Basket

questions.question: Inflation is best defined as:
options: A sustained and significant increase in the GENERAL price level over time
Any increase in the price of bread
A once-off rise in prices after a VAT increase
A fall in the value of the rand against the dollar

questions.question: Inflation falls from 7% to 5%. This is called:
options: Deflation
Disinflation — prices still rising, but more slowly
Stagflation
Hyperinflation

questions.question: The weights in the CPI basket are determined by:
options: The Reserve Bank's inflation target
The prices charged by the largest retailers
Household surveys of what South Africans actually spend their money on
Parliament, when it passes the budget

questions.question: The difference between the CPI and the PPI is that:
options: The PPI includes services and the CPI does not
The CPI is measured yearly and the PPI monthly
The PPI is always higher than the CPI
The CPI measures the cost of living at the till, while the PPI measures the cost of production at the factory gate

questions.question: The base-year trolley cost R4 000; the same trolley now costs R4 480. The index now stands at:
The CPI moves from 112,0 to 118,7 over a year. The inflation rate is:
options: About 6,0% — the 6,7-point change divided by the OLD index of 112,0, times 100

questions.question: A basket has food (weight 50%, up 10%), transport (30%, up 5%) and school costs (20%, up 20%). Weighted inflation is:
A wage rises 4% in a year when inflation is 6%. In real terms the wage has:
options: Risen by 4%
Risen by 10%
Stayed the same
Fallen by roughly 2% — the rand figures grew, but the trolley they can fill shrank

questions.question: Demand-pull inflation occurs when:
options: Total spending grows faster than the economy's capacity to produce — too much money chasing too few goods
Production costs rise and are passed on to consumers
The government fixes prices by law
Imports become cheaper

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY cost-push causes?
options: Cheap credit, consumer booms, export surges
A weaker rand raising import costs, electricity tariff hikes, wage settlements above productivity
Government deficits, investment booms, rising incomes
Falling interest rates and rising grants

questions.question: In the curve story, cost-push inflation is shown by:
options: Aggregate demand shifting right — prices up, output up
Aggregate demand shifting left — prices down
Aggregate supply shifting left — prices up, output DOWN
Both curves shifting right together

questions.question: Stagflation is the combination of:
options: Falling prices and rising output
Rising prices and rising employment
Zero inflation and zero growth
Rising prices together with falling output and rising unemployment

subtopics.title: Consequences and the Fight Against Inflation

questions.question: Inflation redistributes wealth from:
options: Creditors to debtors — loans are repaid in shrunken rands
Debtors to creditors
Borrowers to the government
Property owners to shareholders

questions.question: A saver earns 5% interest while inflation runs at 6%. The real interest rate is:
options: Minus 1% — the nominal rate minus the inflation rate

questions.question: South Africa's inflation-targeting framework requires the Reserve Bank to keep CPI inflation:
options: At exactly 0%
Below the PPI
Inside a band of 3 to 6 percent, using the repo rate as its main instrument
Equal to the growth rate of GDP

questions.question: Why does raising the repo rate work poorly against cost-push inflation?
options: Because banks ignore the repo rate
Because it makes the rand weaker
Because cost-push inflation is not real inflation
Because higher interest rates cannot lower production costs — they only suppress demand, at the price of output and jobs

subtopics.title: The Trolley That Tells the Truth

questions.question: The CPI 'trolley' is filled according to:
options: What surveys show households actually buy, with bigger spending items taking more space
Whatever is cheapest each month
The finance minister's shopping list
Only food and fuel

questions.question: An index reading of 112 means:
options: The trolley costs R112
What cost R100 in the base year now costs R112
Inflation is 112%
Prices fell by 12%

questions.question: Your family's costs rose faster than the official inflation rate. This is possible because:
options: Statistics South Africa only prices luxury goods
The official rate is set by the shops
The official trolley is an average basket, and no household's spending matches the average exactly
Inflation is measured only once a decade

questions.question: The tell-tale sign of demand-pull inflation is:
options: Shops busy, goods selling out, order books full — many hands reaching for few goods
Quiet shops with rising prices
Falling prices everywhere
A stronger rand

questions.question: A drought raises maize prices and electricity tariffs jump. Prices rise while shops stay quiet. This is:
options: Demand-pull inflation
Cost-push inflation — costs pushing prices up from behind, even though customers are not spending more
Deflation
Creeping demand inflation

questions.question: Pointing the repo-rate 'hose' at a cost-push fire mainly:
options: Lowers petrol and electricity prices
Ends the drought
Suppresses spending and jobs while the cost pressure remains
Strengthens wage bargaining

questions.question: Why must an essay say WHICH type of inflation is burning before recommending policy?
options: Because examiners prefer long answers
Because both types have the same cure
Because inflation types change monthly
Because the cure depends on the cause — the repo rate fights demand-pull well and cost-push badly

subtopics.title: Who Wins and Who Loses When Prices Run

questions.question: The clearest LOSERS from inflation are:
options: Pensioners on fixed incomes, savers earning below inflation, and workers without bargaining power
Borrowers with large debts
Owners of property and shares
The government as a debtor

questions.question: Borrowers can quietly gain from inflation because:
options: Banks cancel their debts
They repay their loans in rands that are worth less than the rands they borrowed
Interest rates always fall during inflation
Their salaries are frozen

questions.question: The target band is set at 3 to 6 percent rather than zero because:
options: Zero inflation is impossible to measure
The IMF requires it
A little steady inflation keeps the economy moving, while double digits destroy planning and trust in money
Banks profit from the band

questions.question: Zimbabwe in 2008 illustrates:
options: Successful inflation targeting
Disinflation
The benefits of printing money
Hyperinflation — prices rising so fast that money stopped working and citizens abandoned the currency
